name: gitglasses
description: Free, open-source git toolkit for VS Code and Open VSX: inline blame, Commit Graph, file and line history, commit search, interactive rebase and worktrees. Works on private repos with no account, and your AI agents can use it over MCP.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode GitGlasses runs no git commands, so no program the repository configures (hooks, filters, fsmonitor, diff drivers, ssh commands) can run: blame, commit history and the commit graph are read straight from the repository, while file and line history, patches and every command that changes the repository or contacts a remote stay off until the folder is trusted. Settings that choose an executable, a network endpoint or a link target are read from user settings only.

commands.title: Open Repo Group in New Window
Continue Merge, Rebase, Cherry-pick or Revert
Abort Merge, Rebase, Cherry-pick or Revert

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with GitGlasses
walkthroughs.description: Every feature is free, with no account to create and no telemetry. History, blame and the graph work offline; only integrations you connect, fetch, pull and push, and AI commands go online.

steps.title: Read your history in the Commit Graph
steps.description:
The graph shows branches, merges and authorship together, on public and private repositories alike.
[Show Commit Graph](command:gitglasses.showGraph)
Coming from Git Graph? [Carry your settings over](command:gitglasses.comingFromGitGraph).

steps.title: See who changed a line, as you type
steps.description:
Inline blame annotates the current line. File blame and the heatmap annotate the whole file.
[Toggle Inline Blame](command:gitglasses.toggleLineBlame)

steps.title: Trace a file over time
steps.description:
Visual File History plots each revision by size and author, so churn is obvious at a glance.
[Show Visual File History](command:gitglasses.showFileHistory)

steps.title: Jump to the file on your forge
steps.description:
Open the current file, at the current line, on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket.
[Open File on Remote](command:gitglasses.openOnRemote)

steps.title: Work on two branches at once
steps.description:
Worktrees check out another branch in a separate folder, so you can review a pull request without stashing.
[Add Worktree…](command:gitglasses.worktrees.add)

steps.title: Bring your own AI key, or none at all
steps.description:
Explain a commit, or draft a commit message with the sparkle button in Source Control. Use a model your editor already provides, a local Ollama model, or your own API key. Nothing is metered and nothing is sent to GitGlasses.
[Choose AI Provider…](command:gitglasses.ai.chooseProvider)

steps.title: Connect issues and pull requests
steps.description:
Launchpad gathers your pull requests and issues. Connect a forge or issue tracker, cloud or self-hosted, without editing settings by hand.
[Connect Integration…](command:gitglasses.connectIntegration)

gitglasses.rebaseEditor.enabled.markdownDescription: Open the todo list of an interactive rebase started outside GitGlasses, such as `git rebase -i` in a terminal, in the GitGlasses rebase editor. Git must use VS Code as its editor, for example `git config --global sequence.editor "code --wait"`. Turn it on before git opens the list: git goes on as soon as any editor of the list closes, so reopening a list that is already open as text hands it to git unchanged. Read from user settings only.

enumDescriptions: Annotations and CodeLens follow their individual settings
Distraction-free: hide inline blame, status bar blame, file annotations, and blame CodeLens
Review: gutter blame annotations forced on in the editors you open
gitglasses.mode.description: GitGlasses mode; switch via the status bar item or the Switch Mode command

gitglasses.keyboardShortcuts.enabled.markdownDescription: Turn on GitGlasses keyboard shortcuts: `Ctrl+Alt+G` (`Cmd+Alt+G` on macOS), then `G` Commit Graph, `B` inline blame, `Shift+B` file blame, `H` visual file history, `F` search commits or `C` Git Commands. Off by default, so none of the editor's own shortcuts are taken over. On Windows keyboard layouts where `AltGr+G` types a character, leave this off and bind the commands in Keyboard Shortcuts instead.

gitglasses.currentLine.enabled.markdownDescription: Show blame at the end of the line the cursor is on. **GitGlasses: Toggle Inline Blame** flips this setting. The status bar item follows `#gitglasses.statusBar.blame#` on its own.

gitglasses.currentLine.delay.markdownDescription: Milliseconds the cursor rests on a line before its inline and status bar blame show. After an edit, blame always waits at least 300 ms so typing does not blame every keystroke.

gitglasses.currentLine.format.markdownDescription: Text of the current-line blame. Tokens: `${author}` (author name), `${email}` (author email), `${date}` (author date in the `#gitglasses.blame.dateStyle#` style), `${ago}` (author date, relative), `${summary}` (first line of the message), `${sha}` (short sha).

enumDescriptions: Show the current line's blame in the status bar unless VS Code's own Git blame item (`git.blame.statusBarItem.enabled`, with `git.enabled` on) is showing, so the same line is not described twice
Always show it, next to VS Code's own item if that is on, whether or not inline blame is on
Never show it
gitglasses.statusBar.blame.markdownDescription: Status bar blame for the current line, independent of `#gitglasses.currentLine.enabled#`. Its tooltip shows the full commit like the hover does, and clicking it opens the commit's details. In `auto`, GitGlasses steps aside while VS Code's built-in `#git.blame.statusBarItem.enabled#` is showing (it does not while `#git.enabled#` is off); set this to `show` (and optionally turn the built-in item off) to use the GitGlasses item instead.

gitglasses.statusBar.format.markdownDescription: Text of the status bar blame, with the tokens of `#gitglasses.currentLine.format#`.

gitglasses.hovers.enabled.markdownDescription: Show the blamed commit when hovering a line: author and dates, the full message, the pull request it came from when the message names one, and links to the commit's details and changes, the file before the commit, the sha and the commit on the remote.

enumDescriptions: 3 days ago
Oct 17, 2026 (in your locale)
gitglasses.blame.dateStyle.markdownDescription: How `${date}` renders in the current-line and status bar blame.

gitglasses.blame.ignoreWhitespace.markdownDescription: Ignore whitespace-only changes when attributing lines (`git blame -w`).

enumDescriptions: Attribute moved or copied lines to the commit that moved them, like plain `git blame`
Follow lines moved or copied within the file to the commit that wrote them (`git blame -M`)
Also follow lines moved or copied from other files changed in the same commit (`git blame -C`)
gitglasses.blame.detectMovedLines.markdownDescription: Move and copy detection. Slower on large histories. Needs the git CLI; without it blame works as with `off`.

gitglasses.blame.useIgnoreRevsFile.markdownDescription: Look through the commits listed in the files `blame.ignoreRevsFile` names, or in the repository's `.git-blame-ignore-revs` when that git setting is unset, as GitHub does. A file that does not exist, or that git cannot read (an abbreviated sha, say), is skipped with a note in the GitGlasses output. Needs the git CLI.

gitglasses.views.pageSize.description: Commits loaded per page in the Commits and File History views

gitglasses.graph.pageSize.description: Rows loaded per page in the Commit Graph and Visual File History

gitglasses.graph.maxLanes.description: Most branch lanes the Commit Graph draws side by side. Lanes past it fold into one column marked +N, so commit messages stay readable on merge-heavy repositories. The graph also never takes more than 40% of the panel's width.

gitglasses.codeLens.enabled.description: Show git blame CodeLens above files and top-level symbols

gitglasses.engine.path.description: Path to gitglasses-engine (defaults to the bundled binary)

gitglasses.web.maxRepoBytes.description: Web only: maximum total bytes mirrored into the in-memory wasm engine before GitGlasses aborts with an error (default 200 MB)

gitglasses.engine.logLevel.description: Engine log level (logs go to the GitGlasses output channel)

gitglasses.integrations.hosts.description: Git hosting instances beyond github.com, gitlab.com and bitbucket.org, e.g. [{ "domain": "github.example.com", "provider": "github-enterprise" }]. Azure DevOps takes dev.azure.com plus an organization.

domain.description: Hostname of the instance, e.g. github.example.com

enumDescriptions: GitHub (github.com; any other domain is treated as GitHub Enterprise Server)
GitHub Enterprise Server
GitLab (gitlab.com or self-managed)
Bitbucket Cloud (bitbucket.org only)
Bitbucket Data Center
Azure DevOps Services (dev.azure.com only; needs organization)

organization.description: Azure DevOps organization, e.g. contoso for https://dev.azure.com/contoso

enumDescriptions: Jira Cloud (*.atlassian.net)
Linear
GitHub Issues (github.com unless host names a GitHub Enterprise Server)
GitHub Enterprise Server issues

host.description: Tracker host: the Jira Cloud site (e.g. mycompany.atlassian.net) or the GitHub Enterprise Server hostname

enumDescriptions: Not chosen yet: the first AI command asks which provider to use
A language model another extension provides to the editor, such as GitHub Copilot (VS Code only)
Anthropic Claude API (bring your own key)
OpenAI API or any compatible endpoint (bring your own key)
Google Gemini API (bring your own key)
Ollama: on this machine, no key, nothing sent over the network
gitglasses.ai.provider.markdownDescription: Where GitGlasses AI requests go. Until a provider is chosen, the first AI command offers the ones this editor can use; change it any time with **GitGlasses: Choose AI Provider…**. Saving an API key with **GitGlasses: Set AI API Key…** switches to that provider.

gitglasses.ai.model.description: Model id for the selected AI provider (empty = provider default)
gitglasses.ai.model.markdownDeprecationMessage: Use the per-provider model settings instead, such as `#gitglasses.ai.anthropic.model#`; GitGlasses moves this value there when it switches provider.

gitglasses.ai.anthropic.model.description: Anthropic model id, such as claude-sonnet-5-5 or claude-haiku-5-5 (empty = claude-opus-5-5)

gitglasses.ai.openai.model.description: OpenAI model id, or the model name an OpenAI-compatible endpoint expects (empty = gpt-6-luna)

gitglasses.ai.ollama.model.description: Ollama model name (empty = gemma4 when installed, otherwise the first installed model)

gitglasses.ai.vscodeLm.model.description: Id, family or name of the editor language model to use (empty = the first available, preferring GitHub Copilot)

gitglasses.ai.openai.baseUrl.description: Base URL for OpenAI-compatible endpoints (empty = https://api.openai.com/v1)

gitglasses.autolinks.description: Custom autolink patterns applied to commit messages, e.g. [{ "regex": "TICKET-(\\d+)", "urlTemplate": "https://tracker.example.com/browse/TICKET-$1" }]

regex.description: Regular expression matching the reference text

urlTemplate.description: Target URL; capture groups referenced as $1, $2, …
